result.answer: Trusting the bed manager's times would not settle this. BEDMGR's time is exactly the same as PAS's: both moves have an event time of 08:20 UTC on 15 Oct. PAS sent the patient to WARD-B. BEDMGR sent the patient to WARD-C, bed BAY1-07, and only BEDMGR's move was applied. Neither move is later, so the times cannot show which one replaced the other. The lifecycle rule says that when event times are equal, we cannot tell which move replaced the other. In that case nothing should be applied, and a person must decide. So I cannot say whether PAS's move to WARD-B still holds. The case does not show where the patient really is. What would decide it is trusting BEDMGR's placement, not its times. If the site named BEDMGR as the system that decides ward placement, its WARD-C move would stand. This case would then close with no write instead of going to a person (W1). That setting is not in place now. One small correction to the board: its findings say the bed-management system's epoch is 86, but its record shows 96 (version 2).

response.content: I've submitted my answer: trusting the bed manager's times doesn't settle it, because both moves have the same time, and only naming the bed manager as the system that decides ward placement (W1) would close the case with no write.
